sentences.text: Sosa vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2023
Bench: Surya Kant, J.K. Maheshwari
1  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal No.9830/2013
SOSA & ORS. Appellan
VERSUS  STATE OF KERALA & ANR. Responde  O R D E R
The State of Kerala acquired more than 32 hectares land for the public purpose of installation of Oil Storage Tanks by Indian Oil Corporation (Respondent No.2).
The land was situated in Village Thiruvankulam, Kanayannur Taluk in Ernakulam District.
The Notification under Section 4 read with Section 17 (4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was published on 09111994, followed by Notification under Section 6 of the Act on 31031995.

The Land Acquisition Officer passed the award on 11021997, whereby compensation for dry land was determined @ Rs.33480/ per Are and for wet land, the rate was determined at Rs.4780/ per Are.
2.
The appellants land measuring 62.51 Are comprising dry land and 55.49 Are comprising wet land was also part of the acquisition.
3. The appellants were also awarded compensation as per the rates determined by the Land Acquisition Officer, as referred to above.
The appellants then sought reference under Section 18 of the Act.
The Reference Court made some enhancement in compensation vide award dated 3107 2000.

The matter was further taken up in appeal and the High Court vide Judgment dated 0301 2008, remanded the case to the Reference Court for fresh adjudication, as according to the High Court, the value of the land was required to be determined on appreciation of the entire evidence.
The High Court also directed to appoint a Commissioner for establishing the location and importance of the acquired land.

4. In deference to the High Courts directions dated 03012008, the Reference Court appointed an Advocate Commissioner and on consideration of its Report, the Award dated 30072008 was passed, enhancing the compensation for dry land by 40% instead of 25% as granted earlier and for wet land, it was enhanced to 50% as compared to 40%.
In this manner, the value of the dry land was fixed @ Rs.46872/ per Are and value of the wet land was fixed at Rs.7170/ per Are.

Sosa vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27679487/
1 5.
The appellants were still dissatisfied and hence they again moved the High Court.
Vide impugned Judgment dated 11062010
, the High Court has marginally enhanced the market value of the dry land @ Rs.50,000/ per Are and of the wet land at Rs.11,875/ per Are.
Still aggrieved, the appellants are before this Court.

6. We have heard Shri V. Giri, learned Senior counsel for the appellants, Shri K. Rajiv, learned counsel for Respondent No.2  Indian Oil Corporation and perused the relevant record with their able assistance.
7. The contentious issue that arises for consideration essentially revolves around the determination of the market value of the wet land.

A pointed reference has been made to the concurrent findings of fact to the effect that both the dry land and wet land were lying contiguously and were being enjoyed by the appellants as one composite holding.
The entire land had a direct frontage on the IrumpanamKakkanad road which is presently known as Sea PortAirport Road and was an important thoroughfare even before acquisition.
It has been further held, as a matter of fact, that the wet land was situated by the side of the road and had direct access from the said road.
It has also been found that the acquired wet land was being developed by the appellants side by side.

On this premise, it is urged on behalf of the appellants that no distinction ought to have been drawn between the dry land and wet land for the purpose of determination of the market value, more so,
when the entire chunk of land has been acquired and utilized for the same public purpose.

8. During the course of hearing, learned Senior counsel for the appellants has further pointed out that vide an Award which is stated to be dated 30112000 passed in LAR 3/98 (Thomas J.
Vayalattu & Others vs. State of Kerala & Ors.), learned Reference Court, Ernakulam has awarded compensation @ Rs.31983/ per Are for the wet land.

entities.text:
3/98 (Thomas J.
Vayalattu & Others vs. State of Kerala & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is categorically stated that the abovesaid award pertains to the same acquisition.
It is contended that the appellants are also entitled to compensation for wet land at the same rate as has been awarded by the Reference Court to similarly placed expropriated land owners.

9. Learned counsel for Respondent No.2  Indian Oil Corporation submits that despite his best efforts, he could not ascertain as to whether or not the aforestated award of the Reference Court,
relied upon by the appellants, was challenged in appeal before the High Court and if challenged,
what was the outcome of such appellate proceedings.

10. Having considered the rival submissions, it appears to us that though the wet land cannot be equated with dry land for the purpose of determination of the market value, however, there cannot be any disparity in the rate of compensation for the wet land which is acquired through same acquisition process.

The entire wet land acquired under the subject  acquisition, deserves to be assessed at the same rate, save and except, where specific reasons are assigned to differentiate the potentiality and utility of scattered parcels of the wet land.

In the absence of any such distinction available on record, it appears to us that the rate of wet land of the appellants requires re determination by the High Court, especially keeping in view the award dated 30112000 which according to the Appellants was passed in respect of the same acquisition.

Sosa vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27679487/
2 11.

We, thus, deem it appropriate to remit the case to the learned High Court for redetermination of value of the wet land of the appellants, for which the parties shall be at liberty to raise their respective pleas before the High Court.
12. For the reasons aforestated, the appeal is allowed in part; the impugned Judgment of the High Court dated 11062000 is modified to the extent of determination of the market value of the wet land.

The High Court is requested to redetermine the value of the wet land, taking into consideration the relevant material including the Award dated 30112000 passed by the Reference Court which, as it appears from the record, was not relied upon as an exampler before the High Court at the time of hearing of Land Acquisition Appeal No.99 of 2009 filed by the appellants.

13. The parties are directed to appear before the High Court on 10042023.
14.

Keeping in view the fact that the acquisition pertains to the year 19941995, we request the High Court to decide the appeal preferably within six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
J (SURYA KANT) J (J.K. MAHESHWARI)
NEW DELHI 15TH MARCH, 2023.
